title: D.B. Cooper Hijacking
hook: In November 1971, D.B. Cooper hijacked a plane and vanished, sparking a lasting mystery.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: On November 24 1971, D.B. Cooper boarded a Northwest Orient flight from Portland to Seattle.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: He demanded $200,000 and four parachutes, which were dropped over Seattle's airport.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: At 10,000 feet, Cooper opened the rear door and vanished.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: In 1980, $5,880 of the ransom was found along the Columbia River.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: Investigators think he parachuted into forest, yet no body or gear was recovered.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: A 2016 FBI review noted a skydiving skill, but the case stays open.

end.line: What do you think happened to D.B. Cooper after the jump?

description: Explore the baffling D.B. Cooper hijacking and the lingering mysteries surrounding his disappearance.

facts.claim: The hijacking occurred on November 24 1971 on Flight 305 from Portland to Seattle.
$5,880 of the ransom was recovered in 1980 along the Columbia River near Vancouver, Washington.
Cooper opened the rear door at about 10,000 feet before parachuting.
The FBI closed the case in 2016 without identifying Cooper.
It remains the only unsolved skyjacking in U.S. history.
